div.l: Ther was also a Nonne a Prioresse
That of hir smilynge was ful symple and coy
Hir grettest othe was but by seint loy
And she was cleped / madame Englentyne
Ful wel she song / the seruice diuyne
Entuned in hir nose ful semely
And frenssh she spak / ful faire and fetisly
After the Scole of Stratford atte Bowe
For frenssh of Parys / was to hir vnknowe
At mete wel y taught / was she with alle
She leet no morsel / fro hir lippes falle
Ne wette hir fyngres in hir sauce depe
Wel cowde she carie a morsel / and wel kepe
That no drope / ne fille vpon hir breste
In curtesie was sette / ful moche hir leste
Hir oủrelippe wyped she so clene
That in hir cuppe / ther was no ferthing sene
Of grece whan she / dronken hadde hir draught
Ful semely after hir mete she raught
And sikerly she was of greet disport
And ful plesant / and amyable of port
And peyned hir to countrefete chere
Of court / and to ben estately of man̉ere
And to ben holden / digne of reủerence
But for to speken of hir conscience
She was so charitable / and so pitous
She wolde wepe ȝif she sawe a mous
Kaught in a trappe / ȝif it were ded or bledde
Of smale houndes / hadde she that she fedde
With rosted flessh or mylk or wastel brede
But sore wepte she / ȝif eny of hem were dede
Or ȝif men smote it with a ȝerde smerte
And al was conscience / and tendernesse of herte
Ful semely hir wympel / pinched was
Hir nose was streight / hir eyen grey as glas
Hir mouth ful smal / and ther to softe and rede
But sikerly she hadde a faire forhede
It was almost a spane brode I towe
For hardely she was not vndergrowe
